solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: When unruly clients go and setter's drunk

definitions.text: When unruly clients go and setter's drunk

indicators.note: something drunk is reeling and disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the setter's is 'setter is', which the setter would say as I'M

explanation.surface: Rowdy customers leave the pub while the crossword compiler is sozzled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles CLIENTS GO plus I'M. The whole clue is also the definition: the bell when rowdy drinkers are turned out, and the setter has had a few by then.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlord's call at the end of licensed hours is when customers, unruly or not, must leave the pub.

clue.text: Surrey, for instance, picked up 15

definitions.meaning: a surrey is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle
15 across said aloud is a homophone of gait, the way someone walks

explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is not the county here but a horse-drawn vehicle. GATE (15) sounds like GAIT, and carriage also means bearing or posture.
explanation.definitionFit: A surrey is a kind of horse-drawn coach, and a person's deportment, the way they walk, is called their bearing.

clue.text: He examines pupils' work on vocal artist

parts.note: op, short for opus, means a work

indicators.note: vocal means spoken, so the painter's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Titian was the Venetian painter of the Renaissance

explanation.surface: A teacher marks pupils' homework about a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupils' looks like schoolchildren but means the eye's pupils. 'vocal' makes TITIAN sound like TICIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye specialist tests sight and looks into the eyes of patients to prescribe lenses.

clue.text: Tim sold arms regularly to Muslims everywhere

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: An arms dealer supplies weapons to the Muslim world.
explanation.definitionFit: The worldwide community of believers in the faith of Muhammad is known by the religion's name.

clue.text: Stamp expert's sobbing uncontrollably

indicators.note: uncontrollably means wildly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A philatelist is weeping without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Gibbons is the London stamp dealer and catalogue publisher; 'expert's' stands for 'expert is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Gibbons, the London firm of philatelists, is the best-known name in British stamp collecting.

clue.text: On to which one cold water bird climbs?

definitions.text: On to which one cold water bird climbs?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: climbs in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: Asking what a chilly seabird would scramble on to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbs' turns GREBE to EBERG beneath I and C. The whole clue also asks where a cold seabird might perch.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating mass of ice in the sea is a likely perch for a bird in polar waters.

clue.text: Basic, like the periodic table?

definitions.meaning: fundamental or essential, at the root
the chart lists every chemical element, so it is made of them

explanation.definitionFit: Something fundamental is primary, and the chart of chemistry sets out every element in order.

clue.text: On holiday over in Suffolk

indicators.note: over signals that the letters picked out are read the other way round
in says the letters sit inside the word Suffolk

explanation.surface: Someone away on a break somewhere in the county of Suffolk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to FFO inside sufFOlk, and 'over' turns it round. Suffolk is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is off work is away from the job, as on a vacation.

clue.text: Love and kiss follow soup

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, so O
X is the cross written for a kiss
to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: Romance and a kiss come after the starter.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick brown soup is made from the tail of beef cattle.

clue.text: Do without — selfishly?

definitions.meaning: to give up or abstain from
split as '...', it means acting for oneself

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into FOR EGO, doing things for the self.
explanation.definitionFit: To go without something is to renounce it, and acting for one's ego is acting selfishly.

clue.text: Badger inveterate liar emerging from his shell?

indicators.note: the creature pokes out from the casing of the two words, so its letters are found inside them

explanation.surface: Nagging a habitual fibber until he opens up and stops being so withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like a verb meaning pester, but it is the animal: the honey badger of Africa and Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The honey badger is a fierce burrowing mammal of the weasel family, close kin to the European badger.

clue.text: He raises birds, earning payback for yeoman

indicators.note: earning means taking money in, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a beater on a shoot drives game birds up into the air for the guns
split as pay plus back: a fee is a payment, and back turns it round

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper's helper gets his wages for serving as a farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter splits 'payback' unsignalled into 'pay' and 'back'. A Beefeater is a Yeoman Warder, a ceremonial guard at the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial guards at the Tower of London are formally titled Yeomen Warders, and nicknamed for their supposed beef rations.

clue.text: Inconvenience as is or separately?

parts.note: taken whole, the first word means bother; split into two words, it puts something inside a lavatory chair, a polite 'convenience', and the answer must fit both

explanation.walkthrough: A convenience is a British euphemism for a toilet, and a commode is a chair hiding a chamber pot. Split the answer after IN and it says 'inside a convenience'.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone out or cause them trouble is to inconvenience them, the meaning of the single word.

clue.text: Crude family name, say, seals victory

indicators.note: seals means closes up around, so one piece is shut inside the other

parts.note: e.g., for example, is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'
a victory is a win

explanation.surface: An oil dynasty's surname clinches a win, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ewings were the oil family of the American TV soap Dallas; 'crude' is crude oil, not vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional Texan clan in the soap Dallas made its fortune in oil, so it is a family named in petroleum.

clue.text: Good girls making spectacles of themselves

parts.note: lasses is a northern and Scottish word for girls

explanation.surface: Well-behaved young women nevertheless behaving embarrassingly in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making spectacles of themselves' suggests showing off; the definition is the eyewear.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles are a pair of lenses worn in front of the eyes to correct vision.

clue.text: Those who enjoy cigars did, when let off meat

indicators.note: off means removed, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: Hamlet is a British brand of cigar, so cigar lovers smoked Hamlet

explanation.surface: Cigar smokers lit up once they were allowed out, and then ate meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet is a mild cigar sold in Britain; drop LET from SMOKED HAMLET.
explanation.definitionFit: Cured pork leg flavoured over wood smoke is a cooked meat.

clue.text: See 18
King's universal soul expected shortly in capital

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
atman is the Hindu term for the self or universal soul

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: due means expected, as in the train is due

explanation.surface: A monarch's soul is expected soon in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a variant spelling of Kathmandu, capital of Nepal; the usual form has an H.
explanation.definitionFit: This Himalayan city is the seat of government of Nepal.

clue.text: Events continuing to absorb head of state

indicators.note: to absorb means to take in, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: going on means continuing

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Proceedings carrying on to take in the head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Events' is a plural noun here, matching the hyphenated plural answer; 'head of state' tempts as a single phrase but only its first letter counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Happenings, especially odd or improper ones, are called by this informal plural.

clue.text: Pay barrier to restrict nursing trainees

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the outer pieces take another inside

parts.note: taken as written
to gate a pupil is to confine them as a punishment
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car, so two learners give LL

explanation.surface: A move to cap the number of student nurses in training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing' looks like the trainees' profession, but it is the container signal. To gate a pupil is an old British school punishment, keeping them in.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier on a road or bridge that opens only when travellers pay a fee.

clue.text: Hold head for extra security

parts.note: a lock is a hold in wrestling
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Grip someone's head to keep them safely restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the part: a second fastener that grips a bolt's head to stop it working loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A second fastener screwed down on another keeps a bolt from loosening under vibration.

clue.text: It forms oval cone after energy's spent

definitions.text: It forms oval cone after energy's spent

indicators.note: forms means shapes into something, so these letters are arranged afresh
spent means used up and gone, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A mountain builds its conical shape once its energy is exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spent' removes E from OVAL CONE, leaving OVALCON, and 'forms' rearranges those letters. Read as a whole, the clue also describes the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiery mountain builds a cone of ash and lava, and an extinct one has used up its force.

clue.text: Disputed naval base straddles Cuba's border

indicators.note: straddles means sits astride, so the pieces go round another
disputed means argued over and unsettled, so these letters are put in a different order

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics
C is the international vehicle registration code for Cuba

explanation.surface: A contested naval base sits across the Cuban frontier, as Guantanamo does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disputed' is the anagram signal, and 'base' is the mathematical E, not a military base. C is the code on Cuban cars' international plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A short drape hanging round a bed frame or above a window is a decorative edging.

clue.text: Former storage failure's probably peripheral

parts.note: a flop is a failure

indicators.note: peripheral means on the edge, so the first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: An old storage gadget's breakdown is probably a fault with an add-on device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peripheral' sounds like computer hardware, but takes P and Y from 'probably'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bendy disk once used to save computer files is now obsolete.

clue.text: Small matter in Cern deflected Rhonda

indicators.note: deflected means knocked off course, so the letters scatter

explanation.surface: A minor issue at the Swiss physics lab put a woman named Rhonda off.
explanation.walkthrough: CERN is the European physics laboratory near Geneva, home of the Large Hadron Collider.
explanation.definitionFit: A subatomic particle made of quarks is a tiny piece of matter, studied at the Geneva collider.

clue.text: Abandon good book in shelter

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible, the Good Book

explanation.surface: Ditching the Bible in a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone or something is to desert it.

clue.text: A falcon flies over from Irish Sea isle

indicators.note: over means one piece covers the other, so the reworked letters wrap round another
flies means moves freely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: fm is a dictionary abbreviation for from

explanation.surface: A hawk crosses the water from a small island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' rearranges A FALCON, and 'over' puts that round FM. The Calf of Man is a small island off the Isle of Man, a bird observatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A small islet lies just off the southern tip of the Isle of Man, in the waters between Britain and Ireland.

clue.text: Ring the same destination for caravans

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
as is means unchanged, the same

explanation.surface: Phoning the same place where camel trains end up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caravans' suggests holiday trailers; here they are desert camel trains.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert camel trains head for a fertile spot with water in the sands.

clue.text: To find prominent Athens ruin I'm sent out

definitions.text: To find prominent Athens ruin I'm sent out

indicators.note: ruin means wreck, so the letters of the two words are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
these letters go out of the mix

explanation.surface: A visitor's instructions for locating a famous ruined temple in the Greek capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Take PROMINENT ATHENS and remove the letters of I'M SENT ('out'), leaving PRONATHEN; 'ruin' rearranges them. The whole clue also points at the ruined temple on the Acropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: The great ruined temple of Athena stands on the Acropolis above Athens, its best-known landmark.

clue.text: Head room exists over students' union

indicators.note: over in this clue turns the short word round

parts.note: is means exists
NUS is the National Union of Students in Britain

explanation.surface: Living space at the students' union building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head room' suggests ceiling height; it means a cavity in the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: The sinuses are air-filled cavities in the bones of the face and skull.

clue.text: The old Nipponese capital

parts.note: ye is an old spelling of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe

indicators.note: capital means the leading letter, the one written as a capital

explanation.surface: Japan's former seat of government, as Kyoto once was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city, but it means money and also picks the first letter of Nipponese.
explanation.definitionFit: Money in Japan is counted in this currency, long established there.

clue.text: Gin or meths possibly?

parts.note: these words are what you get by wrecking, or ruining, the seven letters of a word for mums

explanation.surface: Asking whether the drink is gin or methylated spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as wordplay tells you to ruin MOTHERS, and 'possibly' flags that OR METHS is one such result. Mother's ruin is old British slang for gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap spirit blamed for wrecking families in Georgian London earned this nickname.
